overview: Marloes Sands is a long beach of more than a mile on the Marloes peninsula, near the south-western tip of Wales, owned by the National Trust and backed by high cliffs. Layered sandstone and shale fins run out across the sand. The tidal island of Gateholm sits at the western end, with Skokholm out on the horizon.

You reach it on foot from the National Trust car park, about half a mile away, which helps it feel remote even in summer. There are toilets at the car park, but nothing on the beach itself. Timing matters too: the beach is covered at high tide, so plan your visit around low water, when the rocks and pools are fully exposed.

The peninsula is a big draw for wildlife. Boats to Skomer and Skokholm, with their puffins and Manx shearwaters, leave from nearby Martin's Haven. Grey seals pup around the Deer Park in late summer. Gateholm has remains of prehistoric settlement and was dug by Time Team.
suits: Walkers on the Marloes peninsula circuit
Experienced surfers happy with a remote, unpatrolled beach
notFor: Anyone who needs facilities close to the sand
Visitors arriving at high tide, when the beach is covered

text: Marloes is fully exposed to the open ocean and picks up south-westerly swell, so it can have good waves. But it is rocky, remote and unpatrolled, and help is a long walk away.

The rock fins and the tide shape everything here. At low tide the sand opens up into a long stretch broken by outcrops; at high tide the sea reaches the cliffs. Surf only if you are experienced and with others, and check tide times first.

Marloes is a quiet, exposed beach break that rarely gets crowded. It likes a west-south-westerly swell and a north-easterly offshore, and it's best around low tide. The beach curves from south-west to south facing, so north winds are cross-offshore. Submerged rock and bedrock poking through the sand are the main hazards, so look at the beach at low tide before you paddle out. Winter is best and summer is mostly flat. Access is down narrow winding lanes to a cliff-top car park with a short walk down; facilities are minimal.

cards.title: Experienced only
cards.text: Remote, rocky and unpatrolled — not for learners.

cards.label: Conditions
cards.title: South-west swell, low to mid tide
cards.text: The beach is covered at high tide, so plan around low water.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: Rocks, tide and remoteness
cards.text: Rock fins cross the beach and the tide comes up to the cliffs. Further west, Jack Sound has tidal rips.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Marloes Sands car park
practical.text: A National Trust car park about half a mile from the beach.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Toilets at the car park
practical.text: Toilets at the Marloes Sands and Martin's Haven car parks. Nothing on the beach; more in Marloes village.

practical.label: Dogs
practical.title: Allowed, no bins
practical.text: Dogs are allowed, but there are no dog bins, so take waste home. Keep dogs on leads near livestock and on the coast path.

practical.label: Gateholm
practical.title: Tidal island
practical.text: Reachable on foot only at low tide, and the climb is for the sure-footed only.

faqs.q: Is Marloes Sands covered at high tide?
faqs.a: Yes. The National Trust notes that the beach is covered at high tide, so check tide times.

faqs.q: How far is the walk from the car park?
faqs.a: About half a mile from the National Trust car park.

faqs.q: Can dogs go on Marloes Sands?
faqs.a: Yes, but there are no dog bins. Keep dogs on leads around livestock and on the coast path.
Only at low tide, and the climb onto the island is tricky.
